title: TopiCLEAR: Adaptive embedding clustering for interpretable topic discovery from short texts
read_from: arXiv preprint 2512.06694 (published version: Expert Systems with Applications)
subcategory: embedding clustering with adaptive dimensionality reduction
task: Topic discovery from short and informal texts
problem: Embedding-clustering topic methods work well empirically but the link between embedding geometry and interpretable topics is unclear.
architecture: SBERT document embeddings; PCA to D dimensions, normalisation, PCA to K-1 dimensions and GMM (or k-means) for initial clusters; iterative refinement by Adaptive Dimensionality Reduction: Fisher discriminant analysis on the current cluster labels gives a new (K-1)-dimensional space, re-clustered until assignments stop changing; K given by the user.
key_results: LDA nearly fails on short texts (AgNewsTitle AMI 0.042, TweetTopic 0.037).
ProdLDA, ETM and CTM exceed the 7,200-second limit on 100,000 documents (CPU).
strengths: Simple, fast and strong on short informal texts.
Uses human labels plus qualitative sub-topic analysis instead of relying on coherence.

limitations.text: User must set K; CV tends to overestimate the number of topics, so it should not be used alone to choose K.
Benchmark labels may favour methods aligned with the annotation scheme.
One topic per document (hard clustering); no word-level topic distributions.

notes: BERTopic comparison not controlled because it chooses K itself.
